A bitmap as a sorted vector

Source: R/methods.R
zuroar-vector.Rd

A bitmap behaves like sort(unique(v)) kept compressed. length() is the number of values: an integer, or a double above .Machine$integer.max, as for a long vector. min(), max() and range() read the ends without expanding the bitmap; an empty bitmap has none, so they are errors there. as.double() returns every value exactly. as.integer() does too, and is an error when a value is above .Machine$integer.max, rather than giving NA.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
length(x)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
Summary(..., na.rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
as.double(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
as.numeric(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
as.integer(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
format(x, n = 10, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
print(x, n = 10, ...)

Arguments

x

A bitmap.

...

For Summary, further arguments, which must be absent. For the others, ignored.

na.rm

Ignored: a bitmap holds no NA.

n

For format() and print(), how many values to show.

Value

length() returns a single integer or double, min() and max() a single double, range() two, as.double() and as.integer() a vector, format() a string, and print() x, invisibly.

Details

format() and print() never fail: a bitmap whose pointer did not survive saveRDS() prints as a null pointer, and every other function signals zuroar_error_pointer on it.

To loop over the values, use for (v in as.double(x)): R does not let a class define its own iteration.

Examples

x <- roar(c(1, 5, 9, 100000))
length(x)
#> [1] 4
range(x)
#> [1] 1e+00 1e+05
as.integer(x)
#> [1]      1      5      9 100000
x
#> <zuroar> 4 values in [1, 100000]: 1 5 9 100000
